name: Isshiah
overview: Isshiah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as a Korahite. His designation as "the Korahite" places him within the subgroup of Levites descended from Korah, known for their particular roles and heritage within Israel's priestly structure. This affiliation highlights his connection to the Levitical lineage and its religious significance.
namesAndTitles: The name Isshiah means "y-h-v-h forgets," reflecting a Hebrew origin and carrying a meaning that may indicate a spiritual or covenantal dimension, though the name was not given by God according to Scripture. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:6 without additional titles.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Isshiah as a descendant of Korah, linking him directly to the Korahite lineage within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Isshiah's significance lies in his identification as a Korahite Levite, connecting him to a notable Levitical family with specific religious duties in Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles 12:6 situates him among those who contributed to the community and worship life of Israel, underscoring the continuity of Levitical service through generations. Though not extensively detailed, his presence affirms the enduring role of Korahite descendants in God's covenant people.
